sentences.text: 2 2. This appeal is filed by the claimants seeking enhancement of compensation awarded by the tribunal.
3. Heard the learned counsel for both parties.
4. The parties are referred to as per their ranks before the tribunal for the sake of convenience.
5. Learned counsel for the petitioners has submitted his arguments that tribunal has dismissed this petition without assigning any proper reasons.
To substantiate the case of the claimants 2 witnesses are examined as PW1 and PW2.
10 documents got marked as Ex.P-1 to P-10.

The tribunal has not properly appreciated the evidence on record and dismissed the petition, but the tribunal has awarded the compensation of Rs.9,74,000/-, which is not in accordance with law and facts and also decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court and sought for enhancement of compensation and allowing this appeal.

6. As against this, learned counsel for the respondent No.2-insurance company has submitted his arguments that appeal is not maintainable on the ground that respondent No.1 has not appeared before the Court.
At the request of appellant's counsel, notice to respondent No.1 is dispensed with.
Further he has submitted that tribunal has properly appreciated the evidence on record in accordance with law and facts and dismissed the petition.
That there are no grounds to interfere with the impugned judgment and award and sought for dismissal of the appeal.

7. Having heard the arguments on both sides, the following points would arise for consideration:
(1) Whether the appellants have made out grounds to interfere with the impugned judgment and award as to the liability of the insurance company as well as enhancement of compensation?
(2) What order/award?

8. My answer to the above points are:
(1) Partly affirmative (2) As per final order 9.
I have carefully gone through the materials placed by the petitioners.

On the basis of the complaint filed by Rouf Wazir Patel, Solapur Taluka Police have registered the case in Crime No.124/2012 against an unknown driver of the unknown vehicle for the commission of offences punishable under Sections 279, 304A, 427 of IPC and Section 183, 184, 134A, 134B and 177 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.
Thereafter, the police rushed to the spot and conducted the spot mahazar on 26.07.2012.
Police have also conducted inquest panchanama and obtained PM report and recorded the statement of witnesses and also recorded further statement of the complainant-PW1.

On thorough investigation the IO has submitted the charge sheet against the accused Dinesh Pralhad Kamble, who was the driver of the Eicher Tempo bearing No.MH-13/R-4048 for the offences punishable under Sections 279, 304A, 427 of IPC and Section 183, 184, 134A, 134B and 177 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.

sentences.text: Apart from this documentary evidence, one of the claimants is examined as PW1 and another witness is examined as PW2 - Sadashiva Dhyanumali.
PW2 is CW10 in the charge sheet submitted by the IO.
He is an eye witnesses to this incident.

He has clearly deposed in his evidence that on 25.07.2012 at about 10.15 p.m when he was near Katgaon Patil of Tandulwadi Village along with tractor, at that time one motorcycle bearing registration No.MH.13/S.2245 proceeding towards Hyderabad road by his left side of road in moderate speed, by that time one tempo bearing No.MH.13.R/4048 came from opposite side of the said motorcycle, in high speed, rash and negligent manner, came abruptly towards the said motorcycle, dashed to it and caused accident.
Suddenly I found that rider of the motorcycle has sustained severe injuries.
After few days, it came to his knowledge that the injured died on the spot and he was Munna Wazir Patel.
11. During the course of cross-examination of PW.2, it is not disputed that he has not an eye-witness to the incident.
During the course of RW.1, he has clearly stated that he has not challegned the charge sheet submitted by the police.
Even in the examination-in-chief, he has not whispered anything as to documentary evidence pleased by the claimants.
The tribunal has not properly appreciated the evidence on record in accordance with law and facts.
On appreciation and re-appreciation of the evidence on record, it is crystal clear that the alleged accident occurred due to the rash and negligent on the part of the offending vehicle.
RW.1 has clearly stated that as on the date of the accident the policy was in force.
Hence, the Insurance Company is liable to pay compensation.
12. With regard to the enhancement of compensation is concerned, the tribunal has stated that as on the date of the accident the deceased was aged about 40 years.
In the absence of any evidence or proof of income, the notional income has to be assessed as per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
Since the accident has taken place in the year 2012, the notional income has to be taken at Rs.6,500/- p.m. as per chart.

In view of the law laid down by the Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court in National Insurance Co., Ltd., vs. Pranay Sethi and others reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157, to the aforesaid amount, 25% has to be added on account of future prospects as the deceased was aged about 40 years.

sentences.text: Thus, the monthly income comes to Rs.8,125/-.

Out of which, it is appropriate to deduct 1/4th towards personal expenses and therefore,
the monthly income comes to Rs.6,093/- (8,125-2032).

13. As on the date of the accident, the deceased was aged 40 years, as per the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of SARLA VERMA (SMT) & OTHERS VS. DELHI TRANSPORT CORPORATION & ANOTHER, reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121, the multiplier applied to the age group of the petitioner is 15.

15. In addition, the petitioners are entitled to Rs.15,000/- on account of 'loss of estate' and Rs.15,000/- on account of 'funeral expenses'.

18. For the aforesaid reasons and discussions, I proceed to pass the following;
ORDER (a) The appeal is allowed in part.
(b) The judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is set aside.

(c) The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.13,66,749/- along with interest at the rate of 6%
per annum from the date of claim petition till realization.
(d) The respondent Nos.1 and 2 are jointly and severally is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
- 11 - (e) The respondent No.2-Insurance Company is directed to deposit the enhanced compensation within a period of one month from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.

(f) Out of the compensation amount, 50% of the amount shall be kept in fixed deposit in any nationalized bank for a period of three years and thereafter the petitioner are entitled to withdraw the said amount with accured interest thereon.
( g ) Remaining amount shall be disbursed to the petitioners in accordance with law on proper identification.
(h) Draw an Award accordingly.
